meta.label: ESTIMATED title-loan relevance weighting over MEASURED POI counts (Overture/OSM)
meta.measured: all category COUNTS are measured (a sample/lower bound, not a registry)
meta.estimated: the per-category WEIGHTS are a relevance MODEL (judgement), see weights

weight_rationale.gold: collateral + pawn-adjacent culture; strongest title/pawn co-location signal
weight_rationale.vehicle: collateral supply (vehicle dealers/mechanics) — AutoX's core book
weight_rationale.fresh_mkt: informal cash, thin-file market vendors — canonical title borrower; OSM fresh/wet-market count ONLY (the broad Overture retail bucket is scored separately as retail_general, not passed off as fresh markets)
weight_rationale.agri: farm households with seasonal cash gaps (objective #1 stressed segment)
weight_rationale.factory: wage earners / industrial-estate working-class borrower base
weight_rationale.retail_general: the WHOLE Overture retail bucket (every shop type) — broad, undiscriminating footfall signal, so deliberately LOW-weighted (0.5) vs the specific fresh-market and commerce signals
weight_rationale.food_service: restaurants / street food (OSM rest, Overture food) — informal food operators are real demand but the bucket is broad, so it is LOW-weighted (0.5) and kept separate from commerce
weight_rationale.school: household formation / family expenses — softer borrowing trigger
weight_rationale.excluded: finance & pawn = competitor supply (scored in competitor_coverage); hospitality/health/public/professional/logistics/construction not relevant

meta.note: MEASURED counts from branch_occupations.json (Overture) + branches.json k10 (OSM); per category we take MAX of the two samples.
